meta.id_policy: OBL-<PARENT>-<NN>; NN = two-digit sequence in SPEC file order within parent. Array order: parents grouped P, D, N, G (in that group order); WITHIN each group, parent ids are sorted NUMERICALLY (D1 < D2 < ... < D10 < D11 -- NOT lexicographically, where the string "D10" < "D2"); within a parent, NN ascends. Fixed per review DEF-07: the draft's stated policy and its actual array order disagreed (actual order was D-then-P-then-N-then-G, not the stated P-then-D-then-N-then-G), and neither this document nor decisions-input.json anywhere stated the numeric-vs-lexicographic sort rule the true order actually required. obligations-final.json's array is mechanically re-sorted by script to match this stated policy exactly -- not by hand.
meta.parent_choice_policy: When a Section-6 locked decision (D*) and a Section-3 principle (P*) state the same constraint, the Section-6 decision is the parent (SPEC.md L122: 'Builders inherit these without renegotiation.'). A Section-4 non-goal (N*) is parent only when no principle/decision covers the same ground with more operative detail; where a non-goal is itself the most concrete, actionable statement of a constraint (N4 MCP, N5 web UI, N6 stale-promotion, N7 scan read-only, N8 WAL coordination), it is its own parent. Restatements compile ONCE under the chosen parent; every other id is recorded in that obligation's also_stated_by (provenance only, never a second descent, per contract rule 1).
meta.coverage_policy: Every one of the 30 parents (P1-P10, D1-D11, N1-N8, G1) is either (a) the descends_from of >=1 obligation, (b) present in the also_stated_by list of >=1 obligation (a restatement fully absorbed by its operative parent — this satisfies coverage, it is not a silent drop), or (c) explicitly listed in open_questions with a reason, or a combination of (b)+(c) when only part of the parent's text compiles deterministically. See open-questions-draft.md for the (c) items. UPDATE (F1): P6 is no longer a zero-obligation parent -- OBL-P6-01 (DEF-04 fix) now covers its span-instrumentation half; only the trace-export-target half remains in open_questions (OQ-02, narrowed).
meta.signal_policy: All 24 obligations here compile SPEC decisions about how g8 itself must be built -- not gating rules g8's own product runs against a third-party annotated codebase. g8-conflict's real ConflictKind::GovernanceViolation / ContradictoryDecisions variants (g8-core/src/conflict.rs:33-42) are, per their own doc comments, scoped to cross-ConvergenceSpace conflicts today (a Boundary-intent violation / a same-title-different-body Decision, both 'in the remote space'). Applying GovernanceViolation to 'g8's own repo violates g8's own SPEC' is a dogfooding theory: g8's own CLAUDE.md '## What to avoid' section classifies as Intent{kind:Boundary} under D4's own section-to-kind table, so a downstream coding agent's Plan/Capability that violates one of these obligations is structurally identical to 'a plan's substrate forbidden by a Boundary intent' -- just self-scoped rather than cross-space-scoped. Every obligation is therefore marked signal.wiring=compiled_intent_extension (this wiring is not built in v0.1 code; this compile defines it -- see OQ-07) except OBL-G1-01, whose codegraph_vocabulary_drift gate and Levenshtein/prefix algorithm are reused directly from an existing, already-implemented predicate and is marked advisory:true per P9 ('No Codegraph hard dep' -- codegraph_* gates are optional/advisory for g8).
meta.determinism_note: No timestamps, no randomness, no absolute scratch paths inside this artifact. All paths repo-relative. Stable ordering throughout.

descends_from.title: Annotation grammar: magic-comment only in v0.1.
descends_from.why: The R2 survey (§5.1, §7.2) shows that ast-grep's `#[capability($$$)]` pattern works for direct Rust attribute syntax but breaks on `cfg_attr`-wrapped forms (which require `kind: attribute_item + has: {regex}` workarounds). The R1 patterns table (A2) recommends adapting Rust proc-macros to a magic-comment form for cross-language uniformity. R3 §5.1 recommends ingesting AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md alongside inline markers via a uniform extractor. Supporting both forms in v0.1 doubles the extractor surface, the parse-failure mode space, and the test matrix for an unclear win.

params.description: Every Capability/Intent/ConvergenceTest/Decision/Plan annotation must match the magic-comment grammar // @g8.<kind>(key="value", ...), placed immediately before the annotated symbol with no blank line; multi-line forms wrap with // on each line.

convergence_test.check: rg -n '^\s*//\s*@g8\.(capability|intent|convergence_test|decision|plan)\(' <target>. Verified working this session (not ast-grep --pattern, which is broken for this obligation -- see below): against crates/g8-extractor/src/lib.rs (the extractor's own source, containing the grammar string only in doc-comments/rationale text) it correctly returns ZERO matches; against the real fixture examples/rust-service/src/lib.rs it returns exactly the real 8 annotations present (4 capability, 4 convergence_test, lines 12,29,41,51,60,71,83,96), with no false positives or negatives. This rg-based line-regex check is an honest, independent re-implementation of D1's grammar (not a copy of g8-extractor's own ast-grep-rule-file mechanism at lib.rs:259, which is a valid alternative but not needed here -- a regex over comment TEXT is sufficient and simpler than AST matching for a regex-shaped grammar). Fixed per V2/T2 side finding: the original `ast-grep --pattern '// @g8.$KIND($$$ARGS)'` degenerates because Rust's tree-sitter tokenizes `//...` as one opaque line_comment node -- empirically confirmed 227 spurious matches on a real file.
convergence_test.fails_when: an Annotation row exists in the store whose source span does not correspond to a //-prefixed magic-comment line matching the grammar

descends_from.title: Multi-project topology: per-project store + space.toml federation, with cross-store ATTACH for queries.
descends_from.why: R4 §6 Risk 5 documents that SQLite's `ATTACH DATABASE` is the cleanest pattern for cross-store reads. R1 §8.1 Q1–Q4 explicitly defer these decisions to the architect; the per-project default + opt-in space is the lightest path that supports the single-repo and multi-repo use cases without forcing one to behave like the other. Forcing a global store (`~/.g8/projects/...`) couples the user's local fs to `g8`'s data model — bad.

params.description: A Capability annotation's name value must never contain '::'. The `<project>::<name>` cross-reference notation is space-scoped-query syntax only; annotations carry bare kebab-case names, and projects are inferred from Project.root_path at extraction time.
params.post_check: captured $NAME does not match the substring '::'

scope.note: scope.paths is intentionally workspace-wide: Capability annotations (the content checked) may be declared in any of the six crates' source. scope.crates names g8-extractor because that is the crate whose parser/validator a coding agent edits to change how this check runs. Fixed per review DEF-06: dropped the erroneous '*.md' glob present in the original draft -- capability annotations never appear in Markdown (they are code-level magic-comments per D1/D2), so it was overreach, not just an omission.

convergence_test.check: ast-grep --pattern '// @g8.capability(name = "$NAME", $$$REST)' crates/**/*; collect all captured $NAME values
convergence_test.fails_when: any captured capability name contains '::'

rules: Every g8-managed project directory contains .g8/store.db after `g8 init`.

space.toml lists members as relative-or-absolute project directory paths.

convergence_test.fails_when: either file is missing after the corresponding command, or space.toml's members list omits an added project

descends_from.title: `planner_intent_check` composite query: six-CTE SQLite shape as defined in R4 §4.
descends_from.why: R4 §4 provides the full SQL; R1 D2 commits to the principle ("Cuts latency, eliminates partial-state bugs, makes the decision atomic"). Composite-queries-not-verb-chains is principle 2.

params.basis: inferred_from_name_and_context — NOT a verbatim SPEC statement, labeled as inference per review instruction #6
params.inference: D6's locked text (SPEC.md L249) names drift_hints as one of six planner_intent_check composite-query return columns. SPEC.md never states drift_hints' internal computation. This obligation infers -- from the column's name and its co-listing alongside existing_matches/bottlenecks/parked_ideas (all planner fit-check informational surfaces meant to warn a plan-drafting agent before commitment) -- that drift_hints is meant to surface the same declared-vs-wired-edge gap that graph-tool's codegraph_drift_edges verb detects (drift_edges.surql:20-71, reproduced deterministically and confirmed correct by V2/T3 + V2v), applied to g8's own Capability.consumes/produces fields (D2/SPEC.md L98).
params.predicate: declared consumes/produces (from a Capability annotation's consumes/produces lists) with no corresponding resolved wiring — mirrors drift_edges.surql:61-71's WHERE filter (declared>0 AND resolved=0 on either side), reproduced deterministically per V2/T3.
params.caveat: g8's own internal representation of 'this capability's declared consumes resolved to an actual producer' (g8's analog of graph-tool's code_edge table) is NOT confirmed anywhere in the evidence gathered for this compile -- neither E1's original scope (SPEC.md + g8-core/model.rs + conflict.rs + plan.rs) nor this session's additional reads (ARCHITECTURE.md, store_impl.rs) established the exact table/column g8-store uses for this. This obligation's convergence_test is therefore necessarily behavioral (black-box, via the CLI) rather than a direct grep, unlike most other obligations in this set. See OQ-09.

convergence_test.check: construct a fixture Capability with a declared consumes entry and deliberately zero resolved wiring for it; run `g8 scan` then `g8 plan new` against it; inspect the FitReport.drift_hints field of the resulting plan_check JSON output
convergence_test.fails_when: drift_hints does not surface the fixture's unresolved consumes declaration

Two output modes (uniform across all commands): `--output pretty` (default) and `--output json`. Pretty output is human-readable Markdown; JSON output is stable and versioned with `"g8_version": "0.1.0"` in every payload.

descends_from.title: Crate graph: six crates.
descends_from.why: **Locked:** Workspace members: g8-core (no deps on other workspace crates, used by all), g8-store (deps: g8-core), g8-extractor (deps: g8-core), g8-planner (deps: g8-core, g8-store), g8-conflict (deps: g8-core, g8-store), g8 (deps: all of the above). This is a strict DAG with `g8-core` as the root and `g8` as the only sink. No cycles, no diamonds.

params.forbidden: any workspace-internal dependency edge not in required_edges (e.g. g8-core depending on any other workspace crate; g8-store/-extractor/-planner/-conflict depending on g8; any cycle)

convergence_test.check: cargo metadata --format-version1 | jq the workspace members' dependencies and [[bin]] targets; diff the resulting dependency-edge set against required_edges (must be equal, not just a superset); count [[bin]] targets workspace-wide
convergence_test.fails_when: the edge set differs from required_edges in either direction, or the total [[bin]] target count != 1, or that one bin's crate != g8

descends_from.title: AUDIT-before-enforce ergonomics for `g8 init`.
descends_from.why: The AUDIT-before-enforce pattern (`r1 §6.7, E10`) compose cleanly.

params.idempotency: re-running `g8 init` re-applies migrations (no-op if already applied), refreshes the AUDIT report, and leaves enforcement untouched

convergence_test.check: in a scratch dir: run `g8 init`; assert .g8/config.toml has enforcement="off"; run `g8 check --json`; assert enforcement_disabled / exit_code 0; run `g8 init` again; assert enforcement is still "off"; run `g8 init --enforce`; assert enforcement flips to "on"
convergence_test.fails_when: the default after first init is not "off", a second `g8 init` changes an already-set enforcement value, or --enforce fails to flip it to "on"

descends_from.title: In-loop validator: ship `g8 check --json` with a stable JSON contract.
descends_from.why: If anyone wires `g8` into a harness, they get a drop-in. Stable contracts are cheap to maintain and worth shipping early.

convergence_test.check: run `g8 check --json` in (a) a clean store and (b) a store fixture with one known-bad capability; parse stdout as JSON both times
convergence_test.fails_when: stdout is not valid JSON, a required key is missing, exit_code doesn't match the errors array, or a reason value falls outside reason_vocabulary

descends_from.title: Deterministic vs non-deterministic zones (the M1 principle).
descends_from.why: The value of the protocol is in the deterministic gate, not the drafting layer. Mixing zones inside one crate is the failure mode to avoid.

params.rule: all six v0.1 workspace crates are 100% DETERMINISTIC; a non-deterministic zone (e.g. an LLM-drafting g8-plan-draft crate) may exist only as a new, separate workspace member producing a PlanDraft consumed unchanged by g8-planner::plan_check -- it must never be merged into one of the six existing crates.
params.v01_scope: g8-plan-draft does not exist in v0.1; this obligation currently forbids any of the six crates from acquiring non-deterministic behavior, full stop.
params.tokio_note: tokio's absence is not independently enforced by a dedicated rule (per review DEF-11's softer framing -- 'worth discussing', not 'must fix'): D5 already rejects Turso partly for being async-only, and the StoreConnection/RusqliteStore design is synchronous throughout, so tokio is not expected on the enforced synchronous path. Not equivalent to reqwest/rand-style non-determinism (mere presence of tokio primitives doesn't by itself imply non-deterministic behavior the way a network or LLM call does), so no blanket ban was added; flagged here for transparency rather than silently ignored.

convergence_test.check: grep the six crates for `async fn` combined with a network/LLM-client import; grep for control flow keyed on std::time::SystemTime::now() or unseeded RNG state (complements conv-d11-02's dependency-level check); ALSO grep for chrono::Local::now()/chrono::Utc::now() (fixed per review DEF-11 -- g8-store's own Cargo.toml already declares chrono as a real dependency, confirmed via V2/T1's cargo metadata baseline, and the original grep only matched the literal string std::time::SystemTime::now(), missing this)
convergence_test.fails_when: any of the six crates imports a network or LLM client, or contains a code path whose control flow depends on wall-clock time or unseeded randomness

descends_from.title: Deterministic vs non-deterministic zones (the M1 principle).
descends_from.why: The value of the protocol is in the deterministic gate, not the drafting layer. Mixing zones inside one crate is the failure mode to avoid.

deny_list.quote: No LLM calls live inside these crates. (P3, SPEC.md L63)
No LLM calls live inside these crates. (P3, SPEC.md L63)
No LLM calls live inside these crates. (P3, SPEC.md L63)
'100% deterministic' (P3/D11) -- network I/O has unbounded latency and availability failure and is a canonical non-determinism source; one inferential step from the verbatim quote, not itself stated

excluded_by_design.reason: the crate offers deterministic UUID variants (v3/v5) alongside random v4; banning the whole crate is not cleanly grounded in the verbatim text. See OBL-D11-03 for the narrower call-site rule this compiles to instead.

Fixed per review DEF-10 (uuid/rand treated inconsistently in the draft -- same structural shape, different treatment). rand offers a clean deterministic API (StdRng::seed_from_u64, SmallRng::seed_from_u64) alongside non-deterministic default entry points (rand::random(), rand::thread_rng()), structurally identical to uuid's v3/v5-vs-v4 split. Banning the whole crate is no better grounded in D11's verbatim text than banning all of uuid would have been. Narrowed to a call-site rule instead -- OBL-D11-03 already listed rand::random and rand::thread_rng as forbidden patterns even in the original draft, so this fix removes the redundant/inconsistent blanket ban rather than adding new enforcement.

params.surrealdb_note: surrealdb is intentionally NOT in this list -- it is compiled once under OBL-P9-01 (grounded in P9/N1's own verbatim text) per contract rule 1 (restatements compile once under the most operative, textually-grounded parent).
params.fastrand_getrandom_note: fastrand and getrandom remain on the flat deny_list (NOT given the same carve-out as rand/uuid) because they are not equally analogous: fastrand's entire public API is built around an implicit thread-local global RNG with no ergonomic seeded/deterministic entry point to allow-list, and getrandom is a raw OS-entropy binding with no deterministic mode at all by design. A blanket crate-level ban is the only available deterministic check for these two.
params.known_limitation: Per review DEF-15: this check (cargo metadata dependency-graph inspection) can only prove absence of a DECLARED dependency; it cannot detect non-deterministic code vendored directly into a crate's source tree (e.g. a hand-copied HTTP client with no Cargo.toml entry). OBL-D11-01's complementary grep is also blind to this if the vendored code uses blocking I/O with no matching literal import string. No fully deterministic, complete check for 'no non-deterministic behavior anywhere' is achievable from the current evidence -- 'no declared usage of named libraries' is the closest provable approximation. See OQ-08.

convergence_test.check: cargo metadata --format-version1 | jq '.packages[].dependencies[].name' restricted to the six workspace crates' dependency trees; diff against deny_list
convergence_test.fails_when: any denied crate name appears in the resolved dependency tree of any of the six crates

descends_from.why: The value of the protocol is in the deterministic gate, not the drafting layer. Mixing zones inside one crate is the failure mode to avoid.

params.description: Added per review DEF-11: std::collections::HashMap/HashSet use a per-process-random SipHash seed by default, so iteration order is not stable across runs even for byte-identical input -- a language-runtime non-determinism hazard distinct from any importable-library hazard, and undetectable by OBL-D11-01/02's dependency- and grep-based checks. Forbidden as a field type or intermediate collection on any path feeding --output json/--output pretty (D10) or a composite-query return column (D6), unless immediately converted to a sorted Vec, BTreeMap, or IndexMap before being serialized/rendered.
params.exempt_if: followed by an explicit .sort()/sorted conversion, or replaced with BTreeMap/IndexMap

descends_from.title: No automatic stale-promotion of plans.
descends_from.why: - **No automatic stale-promotion of plans.** The scanner *proposes* promotions; humans approve.

params.description: The `g8 scan` code path must never itself write a Plan status transition (e.g. Parked -> Scoped/Dispatched); status-mutating writes may occur only inside the dedicated `g8 plan promote` command handler, which is human-invoked.
params.forbidden_fn: run (crates/g8/src/cmd/scan.rs:13, the scan command's entry point)
params.allowed_fn: plan_promote (crates/g8/src/cmd/plan.rs:237, the only fn allowed to write a Parked -> non-Parked transition)
params.glob_fix_note: Fixed per review checklist-row-5 finding (not a numbered DEF- entry, found in the per-checklist-verdicts table): forbidden_glob/allowed_glob held prose descriptions ('g8 scan command handler / scanner module'), not real globs or function references. Replaced with the real file:line/fn names, confirmed by direct read this session.

convergence_test.check: ast-grep search for plan-status-mutating calls reachable from the scan command's call graph, as opposed to the plan promote command's
convergence_test.fails_when: a status-mutating write is reachable from `scan` outside the `plan promote` handler

descends_from.title: No modification of target codebases during `scan`.
descends_from.why: - **No modification of target codebases during `scan`.** `g8 scan` is read-only; only `g8 plan new` and `g8 init` write to `.g8/`.

params.scope_fix_note: Fixed per review checklist-row-5 finding: the draft's rule text claimed a broader forbidden_target ('any file under .g8/, except read access') than convergence_test conv-n7-01 actually verifies (store.db hash only). Narrowed the rule's claim to match what is actually tested, rather than expanding the test to hash-check the whole .g8/ directory (which could false-positive on legitimate scan-time artifacts this compile has no evidence about, e.g. logs or caches). Other .g8/ files have their own dedicated checks elsewhere: .g8/INTENT_SUMMARY.md is covered by OBL-D4-02, .g8/config.toml's enforcement flag by OBL-D9-01.

convergence_test.check: sha256sum .g8/store.db before running `g8 scan`; run `g8 scan`; sha256sum again
convergence_test.fails_when: the two hashes differ

descends_from.title: No cross-process write coordination beyond SQLite's WAL.
descends_from.why: - **No cross-process write coordination beyond SQLite's WAL.** Two concurrent `g8` invocations on the same store are safe up to SQLite's `busy_timeout`; beyond that, we error loudly rather than corrupt. (per R4 §6 Risk 2)

requirements: rusqlite connection sets a busy_timeout pragma.
On SQLITE_BUSY persisting beyond busy_timeout, the error must propagate to the caller (loud failure), never be swallowed or silently retried forever.

convergence_test.check: grep g8-store's connection-setup code for journal_mode and busy_timeout pragma calls; integration test: open two connections to the same store.db, hold a write lock past busy_timeout on one, assert the second returns an Err
convergence_test.fails_when: either pragma is absent, or the contended second connection does not return a propagated error

descends_from.title: Glossary.
descends_from.why: ## 5. Glossary — bolded terms defined verbatim: **Annotation**, **Capability**, **Intent**, **Plan**, **ConvergenceSpace**, **Project**, **Substrate**, **Owner**, **FitReport**, **Conflict**, **Annotation grammar**. Plan lifecycle enumeration (embedded in Plan entry): `Idea → Scoped → Dispatched → Blocked → Done | Parked`.

params.similarity_predicate: levenshtein(candidate, canonical) <= 2 OR starts_with(candidate, canonical) OR starts_with(canonical, candidate)
params.predicate_source: graph-tool vocabulary_drift.surql:46-50, reproduced deterministically (not via a live SurrealDB instance, per P9 no-SurrealDB / no-Codegraph-hard-dep)
params.scope_of_candidates: any new struct/enum/type name introduced in g8-core, and this obligation set's own load-bearing vocabulary (title/rule.kind/signal.gate/glossary-adjacent identifiers) Existing-type citations inside another obligation's rule.params (e.g. a real function signature quoted for provenance, such as OBL-D6-01's 'PlanDraft') are citations, not newly-introduced identifiers, and are out of scope by definition, in addition to the explicit allowlist above.
params.allowlist_reason: Real, SPEC-mandated or evidence-confirmed derived types (Canonical+Suffix pattern: <Term>Status/<Term>Kind/<Term>Draft) that legitimately prefix-collide with a canonical term under the raw predicate. Fixed per review DEF-01 (PlanStatus/CapabilityStatus/AnnotationKind/IntentKind collide with Plan/Capability/Annotation/Intent -- confirmed by direct read of g8-core/src/{plan,model,annotation}.rs) and DEF-12 (this obligation set's OWN OBL-D6-01.rule.params.function field cites 'PlanDraft', which would otherwise self-flag under the artifact's own vocabulary_lock scope). DecisionStatus (model.rs:264-270) added proactively for consistency -- same derived-suffix shape, not yet cited elsewhere in this artifact but would collide identically if it were.

excluded_glossary_term.reason: SPEC Section 5's 11th glossary entry is a two-word process-noun (the magic-comment syntax itself), not a candidate Rust type/struct/enum identifier, so it cannot be sensibly Levenshtein/prefix-compared against code symbol names the way the other 10 terms are. Disclosed per review DEF-13; not silently dropped.

params.known_accepted_gap: The predicate (Levenshtein<=2 OR starts_with either direction) is reused VERBATIM from graph-tool's real vocabulary_drift.surql:46-50 (contract rule 5: real predicates only, not an improved reinvention). It catches suffix-append drift (ClaimDraft, CapabilityDraft) but NOT prefix-qualifier drift (RawCapability, SubPlan, MetaIntent -- Levenshtein distance 3, over threshold, and starts_with fails both directions since the strings diverge at character 0). Accepted as a known gap per review DEF-16, consistent with a periodic manual-triage backstop for exactly this class of miss -- a false negative here is lower-stakes than diverging from the real, evidenced algorithm.

convergence_test.check: run a small deterministic script implementing levenshtein<=2 OR prefix-match against every new type/struct/enum name added to g8-core (and against this obligation set's own vocabulary) vs. the 10 canonical terms
convergence_test.fails_when: any candidate name NOT in rule.params.allowlist satisfies the similarity predicate against a canonical term without being an exact match to it (e.g. Capabilty levenshtein=1; CapabilityDraft prefix-match). A baseline-vs-new-commit diff mechanism for what counts as 'new' remains undefined -- see OQ-10.
